source.title: Understanding Sparse Feature Updates in Deep Networks using Iterative Linearisation

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests training outcomes under controlled feature-update frequency and reports both low training error and conditions with poorer generalization; this refines the broad training claim but does not test most listed versions directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR-10 training accuracy reaching 100% for finite feature-update intervals, but the main claim versions concern other mechanisms or benchmarks. It does not test random-label memorization, model width, bad local minima, depth/initialization recipes, above-stability learning rates, or batch-normalization speed.
record.test_reason: The standard-training control uses gradient descent on a ReLU CNN on CIFAR-10 and is included in the reported convergence to 100% training accuracy, bearing on V1. The main feature-learning and generalization comparisons do not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that infrequent feature updates can match SGD test performance in the tested settings, that some feature learning is needed for good generalization, and that damping can improve generalization. Convergence to 100% training accuracy is a supporting observation rather than their central conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces iterative linearisation, which periodically freezes the Jacobian/features while optimizing a linearised network; compares this with standard training. Uses a modified LeNet and ResNet18 on CIFAR-10, not the original studies’ random-label memorization recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature-update frequency K changes feature learning and generalization; ResNet runs with BatchNorm are more sensitive because the normalization layers are linearised. The K = ∞ comparison uses a higher learning rate for computational reasons.

fits_no_version.finding: Sparse feature updates can retain comparable test accuracy, while fixed features and fully solving each linearised problem can generalize worse despite fitting training data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature-update frequency affects generalization separately from training-data fit.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing Gauss-Newton damping improves test RMSE in the one-dimensional regression experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Damping affects the generalization of Gauss-Newton-trained regression networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Linearising BatchNorm makes large-K ResNet runs more prone to divergence; the comparisons also change augmentation, learning rate, and K.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Freezing linearised normalization layers can destabilize iterative-linearisation training.

record.problems: Most experiments are single runs on smaller architectures and CIFAR-10 only; the authors state results may not generalize to transformers or larger models. No uncertainty intervals are reported. Several plotted outcomes are presented as figures without exact numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying rows were omitted; accuracy comparisons not reporting a separate training-error outcome were not included.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; systematic model-size comparisons; substantial training error under early stopping or regularization. Random initialization is not explicitly documented.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error comparisons across depth, identity shortcuts, and special initialization recipes.
Initialization-dependent signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold, curvature dynamics, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability training.
Controlled comparisons of training speed or learning-rate tolerance with and without batch normalization, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the proposed V1 limits_scope verdict for R3: an alternative optimization procedure and untested datasets do not establish a failure of V1. Generalization differences do not challenge a claim about training classification error.

versions.untested_parts: Tests CIFAR-10 train accuracy reaching 100% for finite K in a LeNet variant and compares training with different feature-update frequencies. Does not test CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, width, smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes.

rows.note: The authors state that by the time a finite-K run converges, it has reached 100% train accuracy; the result is reported across finite K rather than separately for each value.
rows.check: For K>1, this reports the proposed iterative-linearisation method's performance, rather than ordinary SGD or Adam training of the nonlinear CNN specified by V1. Separate K=1 into R1. Write the intervals as 10^3, 10^5, 10^6 and 10^7. Appendix C also says Figure 5 uses optimal early stopping, which should accompany the convergence description.
